name: RT-2 — Vision-Language-Action Models (paper summary)
observations: Source: 'RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control', Brohan et al., Google DeepMind, 2023 (arXiv:2307.15818v1), 26 pages, local pdf/embodied_ai_papers.

Core thesis: a single end-to-end model can both map robot observations to actions AND inherit web-scale vision-language knowledge. Achieved by co-fine-tuning a pretrained VLM (PaLI-X 5B/55B, PaLM-E 12B) on robot trajectories plus the original Internet-scale VQA/captioning data, with NO new parameters and no action-specific layers.

Key trick — actions as text tokens: the action is an 8-dim vector (delta x/y/z end-effector translation, delta rot x/y/z, gripper extension, terminate flag). Each continuous dim is discretized into 256 uniform bins, and the vector is serialized as a space-separated integer string, e.g. '1 128 91 241 5 101 127'. This lets actions share the exact same output space and loss as language tokens.

Token reservation: 256 tokens are reserved as action tokens. PaLI-X already has unique tokens for integers up to 1000, so bins map directly to integer tokens; PaLM-E instead overwrites its 256 least-frequently-used tokens (a form of symbol tuning, per Wei et al. 2023).

Training data format: standard VQA phrasing 'Q: what action should the robot take to [task instruction]? A: <action tokens>'. Robot data inherited from RT-1: 13 robots, 17 months, office kitchen, ~7 skills (pick, move near, place upright, knock over, open/close drawer, place into / pick from receptacle). Robot data weighted to ~50% of the PaLI-X training mixture.

Ablation findings: (1) co-fine-tuning with web data beats fine-tuning on robot data only — preserves prior concepts and improves generalization; (2) training a large model from scratch performs very poorly even at 5B; (3) bigger is better — 55B generalizes better than 5B.
Constrained decoding: when prompted with a robot-action task, the model only samples the 256 valid action tokens; on language/VQA tasks it keeps the full natural-language vocabulary.
Real-time inference: 55B model served on a multi-TPU cloud service queried over the network, running at 1–3 Hz; the 5B variant runs ~5 Hz; one service can drive multiple robots.

Results (6k real-world evaluation trials): seen-task performance matches RT-1, but generalization to novel objects/backgrounds/environments is ~2x better than RT-1 and MOO and ~6x better than VC-1/R3M representation baselines. Emergent skills (symbol understanding, visual/math/multilingual reasoning, human recognition) exceed the best baseline by >3x on average.

Chain-of-thought variant: data augmented with 'Instruction: ... Plan: <natural-language plan>. Action: <action tokens>' and fine-tuned for a few hundred steps. Enables multi-stage semantic reasoning (e.g. improvised hammer -> pick a rock; 'I'm hungry' -> pick rxbar chocolate; 'bring me a drink' -> pick 7up).
Also validated on the open-source simulated Language-Table benchmark: RT-2-PaLI-3B scored 90 vs 77 (LAVA), 74 (RT-1), 72 (BC-Zero), suggesting the recipe transfers across robots/simulators.

Stated limitations: web pretraining adds semantic/symbolic understanding but NOT new motor skills — physical repertoire stays bounded by the robot dataset; inference compute is a real-time bottleneck at high control rates (quantization/distillation suggested); few sufficiently capable open VLMs with usable fine-tuning APIs existed at publication (LLaVA cited as a hoped-for open option).

name: LeRobot — current best-practice stack for VLA robotics workflows
observations: Verified via Context7 (library ID /huggingface/lerobot, v0.6.1, High reputation, 4543 code snippets). LeRobot is the most directly relevant modern open-source implementation of the RT-2-style vision-language-to-action workflow.

Architecture of the stack: 'datasets + policies + envs + robot control' unified by a few abstractions — LeRobotDataset (episode-aware storage of video/images + actions + state, loadable from HF Hub or disk), PreTrainedPolicy subclasses, Processors (composable transforms dataset -> policy -> robot), and a shared action/observation contract so sim and real hardware swap cleanly.
Available policies (RT-2 lineage included): ACT, Diffusion, SmolVLA, Pi0 (pi0), Pi0.5, Wall-X, X-VLA, VQ-BeT, TD-MPC. All inherit PreTrainedPolicy and can be pushed/pulled from the Hugging Face Hub.

SmolVLA is the closest conceptual successor to RT-2's recipe: a pretrained VLM backbone (SmolVLM: SigLIP vision encoder + language model) augmented with a separate action expert. The expert cross-attends layer-by-layer to cached VLM K/V, and actions are generated by flow matching with Euler denoising (num_steps default 10) over action chunks. Trainable knobs: num_vlm_layers=16, num_expert_layers, expert_width_multiplier=0.75, chunk_size.

Efficiency pattern that maps onto RT-2's 'keep the VLM, add little else': SmolVLA defaults to train_expert_only=True, which freezes the entire VLM (requires_grad=False, eval mode) so only the action expert plus state/action/timestep projections train. Alternative mode freezes only the lm_head, final norm and last layers. load_vlm_weights=true warm-starts from the pretrained VLM.

Pi0/Pi0.5 give a larger flow-matching VLA option: lerobot-train --policy.type=pi0 --policy.pretrained_path=lerobot/pi0_base, with flags compile_model, gradient_checkpointing, dtype=bfloat16, freeze_vision_encoder, train_expert_only.
SmolVLA fine-tune example: lerobot-train --policy.path=lerobot/smolvla_base --dataset.repo_id=<user>/mydataset --batch_size=64 --steps=20000 --output_dir=outputs/train/my_smolvla (~4h on one A100).

Data collection best practice: lerobot-record with a follower arm plus leader teleoperation, e.g. --robot.type=so101_follower --teleop.type=so101_leader --dataset.repo_id=<user>/<dataset> --dataset.single_task='Grab the black cube' --dataset.num_episodes=5 --dataset.streaming_encoding=true, then dataset.push_to_hub(). This is the practical equivalent of RT-2's 'instruction-annotated demonstration trajectories'.

Deployment / control-frequency solution (RT-2's multi-TPU cloud serving analogue): asynchronous inference with RobotClient + RobotClientConfig (server_address, policy_type='smolvla', pretrained_name_or_path, actions_per_chunk=50, chunk_size_threshold=0.5), plus Real-Time Chunking (--inference.type=rtc) where a background thread produces action chunks while the control loop consumes the previous chunk — explicitly recommended for large, slow VLAs (Pi0, Pi0.5, SmolVLA) to get smooth continuous motion despite inference latency.
CLI surface: lerobot-record, lerobot-train, lerobot-eval, lerobot-teleoperate, lerobot-calibrate, lerobot-find-port, lerobot-setup-motors, lerobot-replay.

Caveat: OpenVLA (the well-known open reproduction of the RT-2 recipe) is not indexed in Context7, so its API was NOT verified in this research pass — do not cite OpenVLA function/class names from memory; consult its GitHub repo directly.
